Use [`MoveEnterDirective`](/docs/reference/move-enter-directive) when an element should animate once, as Angular creates it: a card that fades up, a toast that slides in, a heading that rises. This is the smallest useful piece of Angular Movement.

## Animate an element when it enters

:::code card.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-card',
  imports: [MoveEnterDirective],
  template: `<article moveEnter="fade-up">Billing summary</article>`,
})
export class Card {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/enter.ts#L10-L15)

`moveEnter` takes a [preset name](/docs/presets) or your own keyframes. It runs **once**, when the directive initialises, and ignores later input changes. That is by design: it describes an entrance, not a state. To animate between states when a signal changes, use [reactive animation and variants](/docs/guides/variants).

::playground[enter]

The playground wraps the directive in a small component. Because `moveEnter` is init-only, changing a control (or pressing **Replay**) recreates the element, which plays the animation again — the page is not pretending the directive is reactive. [Open the full playground](/demos/enter) for every preset.

## Shape the timing

Duration, delay and easing are plain inputs shared by every directive. A bare number is milliseconds; a string states its unit.

:::code toast.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-toast',
  imports: [MoveEnterDirective],
  template: `
    <div moveEnter="slide-up" moveDuration="300ms" moveDelay="100ms" moveEasing="ease-out">
      Saved
    </div>
  `,
})
export class Toast {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/enter.ts#L19-L28)

Defaults for the whole app come from [`provideMovement`](/docs/reference/provide-movement); the input on the element always wins.

## Use your own keyframes

Presets are shorthand for keyframes. Pass an object to animate anything the Web Animations API can animate — keyframes are typed for the common shorthands (`x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotate`, `blur`, `opacity`, …) and any other CSS property passes straight through.

:::code wipe.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-wipe',
  imports: [MoveEnterDirective],
  template: `
    <!-- Any CSS property the Web Animations API can animate, not just presets. -->
    <div [moveEnter]="{ clipPath: ['inset(0 100% 0 0)', 'inset(0 0% 0 0)'] }">Wipe</div>
    <div [moveEnter]="{ opacity: [0, 1], y: [16, 0] }" moveDuration="400ms">Rise</div>
  `,
})
export class Wipe {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/enter.ts#L32-L41)

## Let an element finish leaving

[`MoveLeaveDirective`](/docs/reference/move-leave-directive) describes an exit, but it cannot hold a node that Angular has already removed. `@if` destroys its view synchronously, so there is nothing left to animate. Wrap the content in `*movePresence`, which keeps the view in the DOM until every leave animation inside it has finished:

:::code details.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-details',
  imports: [MovePresenceDirective, MoveEnterDirective, MoveLeaveDirective],
  template: `
    <button type="button" (click)="open.set(!open())">Toggle</button>

    <ng-container *movePresence="open()">
      <aside moveEnter="fade-up" moveLeave="fade-down">Details</aside>
    </ng-container>
  `,
})
export class Details {
  protected readonly open = signal(false);
}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/enter.ts#L45-L58)

See [Presence](/docs/guides/presence) for the full model, including keyed lists.

## `[move]` and `moveAnimate`

[`MoveAnimateDirective`](/docs/reference/move-animate-directive) (`[move]`, `[moveAnimate]`) is the shorthand for an entrance plus an exit on one element, with `moveInitial` and `moveExit` states. Like `moveEnter` it is one-shot.

:::code hero-title.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-hero-title',
  imports: [MoveAnimateDirective],
  template: `<h1 [moveInitial]="{ opacity: 0, y: 24 }" [moveAnimate]="{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }">
    Hi
  </h1>`,
})
export class HeroTitle {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/enter.ts#L62-L69)

## Limits to know

- Both directives are no-ops on the server and start after hydration. For an above-the-fold entrance that must paint before the app boots, use CSS; see [Accessibility and troubleshooting](/docs/accessibility).
- Reduced motion jumps straight to the end state automatically.
- Unsure which directive to pick? [Choose an API](/docs/api-selection).
